title: Grant to IMF's Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust
what_it_is: Grant to IMF's Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust

sections.label: IMF global liquidity and SDR
sections.summary: Since the pandemic, the IMF deployed US$1 trillion in global liquidity and reserves through lending and SDR allocation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Since the pandemic, it has deployed US$1 trillion in global liquidity and reserves through lending and allocation of Special Drawing Rights (SDR).

sections.label: IMF requests Singapore contribution
sections.summary: The IMF requested Singapore contribute 21 million SDR, equivalent to US$28.6 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The IMF has requested that Singapore provide a contribution of 21 million SDR, equivalent to US$28.6 million.

sections.label: Singapore contribution to Somalia debt relief
sections.summary: In 2021, after Parliament's approval, Singapore contributed SDR 0.68 million, about US$0.93 million, to Somalia's debt relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In 2021, following Parliament's approval, Singapore contributed SDR 0.68 million, approximately US$0.93 million to Somalia's debt relief.

sections.label: IMF requests Singapore contribution for Sudan
sections.summary: For Sudan, the IMF requested Singapore contribute 4.48 million SDR, approximately US$6.1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: For Sudan, the IMF has requested Singapore to contribute 4.48 million SDR, equivalent to approximately US$6.1 million.

sections.label: Funding sources for PRGT and PRG-HIPC
sections.summary: The PRGT contribution draws from Singapore's SDR allocation, reducing MAS' OFR by 21 million SDR, while the PRG-HIPC Trust contribution does not affect MAS' OFR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Against this, our contribution to the PRGT will thus draw from Singapore’s allocation of the SDR, resulting in a reduction of MAS’ OFR by a relatively modest 21 million SDR, approximately US$28.6 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The contribution to the PRG-HIPC Trust will be funded from Singapore’s share of IMF’s existing resources in IMF accounts and will not affect the size of MAS’ OFR.

sections.label: Motions on MAS grants to PRGT
sections.summary: The Motions propose MAS may give a maximum of 21 million SDR, about US$28.6 million, to the PRGT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The present Motions propose that the maximum amount of grants that MAS may give to the PRGT is 21 million SDR, or approximately US$28.6 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Is this limit inclusive of the previous amount of 14.5 million SDR, approximately US$20 million, that this House passed in a 2016 Motion?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: More broadly, how have Singapore’s past contributions been utilised and how does our cumulative contribution compare with countries of similar size or income levels?

sections.label: MAS contributions accounting and safeguards
sections.summary: Questions ask how MAS accounts for contributions, safeguards against erosion, materiality thresholds, and RST exposure limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Second is, how are these contributions accounted for within MAS’ balance sheet and what safeguards are in place to ensure that repeated contributions do not lead to structural erosion over time?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Third, at what point, if any, would the cumulative size or frequency of such contributions be considered material from a reserves-management perspective, and does MAS apply internal thresholds or stress scenarios in this regard?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But as the RST is designed to provide longer-term financing for climate and structural resilience, can the Minister also clarify whether MAS expects Singapore’s loan exposure under the RST to grow over time and what internal limits or review mechanisms are applied to ensure that such commitments remain consistent with our overall reserves-management framework?

sections.label: MAS media releases transparency
sections.summary: MAS would issue media releases for each contribution for transparency and accountability, though reach to ordinary Singaporeans is uncertain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While MAS would issue media releases for each of our contributions to ensure greater transparency and accountability, I am not sure how effective these media releases would be in reaching ordinary Singaporeans.

sections.label: IMF PRGT and Sudan grant support
sections.summary: The Motions seek approval for grant support of about S$36 million for the IMF's PRGT and under $8 million for Sudan.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Motions seek approval for grant support from the IMF's PRGT to the tune of around S$36 million for the trust fund, and a little less than $8 million for Sudan.

sections.label: Singapore PRGT pledges drawdown status
sections.summary: As of 2025 Singapore's PRGT pledges totalled $1.25 billion, and the Minister is asked if earlier amounts were drawn down.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To this end, I note that as of 2025, Singapore's pledges to the PRGT amounted to $1.25 billion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Would the Minister of State clarify the status of the prior pledged amounts, specifically, has part or all of the earlier $1.25 billion been drawn down already, which justifies this additional injection?

sections.label: Amounts capped and Parliament-approved
sections.summary: The amounts are capped, specified and approved by Parliament, which is appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The amounts are capped, specified and approved by Parliament, which is appropriate.

sections.label: Singapore giving more than others
sections.summary: Singaporeans may ask whether Singapore is giving more than others while many countries turn inward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Even so, Singaporeans may reasonably ask whether Singapore is giving more than others at a time when many countries are turning inward.

sections.label: Other countries' trust contributions
sections.summary: Asks how much other countries contribute to the two trusts and how Singapore's contribution compares.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can the Government share how much other countries are contributing to these two trusts and how Singapore's contribution compares with theirs?

sections.label: Support for IMF PRGT grant
sections.summary: A Member states support for the motion to provide a grant to the IMF's Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, I support the motion to provide grant to IMF's Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust (PRGT).

sections.label: PRGT role for vulnerable economies
sections.summary: The PRGT provides timely and concessional financing to vulnerable economies at the onset of crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The PRGT plays a critical role by providing timely and concessional financing to vulnerable economies at the onset of crisis.

sections.label: Measured contribution, multilateral amplification
sections.summary: The contribution is measured and controlled, and its impact is amplified through a multilateral framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, our contribution is measured and controlled, and its impact is amplified through a multilateral framework.

sections.label: Measured contribution, multilateral amplification
sections.summary: The contribution is measured and controlled, and its impact is amplified through a multilateral framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, our contribution is measured and controlled, and its impact is amplified through a multilateral framework.

sections.label: Pressures on low-income countries
sections.summary: Low-income countries face high debt, weak growth and limited fiscal space, and without concessional financing risk instability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Today, many low-income countries face the combined pressures of high debt, weak growth and limited fiscal space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Without concessional financing, they have to be forced into shortcuts to essential services or disorder defaults, creating broader financial and social instability.

sections.label: SDR loan to IMF RST
sections.summary: MAS updated that 746 million SDR will be loaned to the IMF's RST, with only 23 countries contributing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Second, as noted by my colleague, Mr Saktiandi: although not required for Parliamentary approval, MAS has updated that 746 million of SDR will be loaned to the IMF’s RST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This does not seem like a small sum in both absolute terms and as a proportion of our total SDR on our balance sheet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: According to the IMF’s website, only 23 countries have contributed to this trust.

sections.label: Clarifications on grants
sections.summary: The grants do not draw on Past Reserves, do not reduce domestic spending, and are channelled through IMF trust funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, I seek to clarify that these grants do not constitute a drawdown of Past Reserves, and they do not trigger the Reserves spending threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, that these contributions do not replace or reduce domestic spending on healthcare, housing, education or cost-of-living for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Third, that these grants are not bilateral transfers to an individual government but are channelled through established IMF trust funds with clear governance, accountability and oversight.

sections.label: Pledges to IMF trusts
sections.summary: Over 40 countries have pledged to the PRGT and more than 120 to the PRG-HIPC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Over 40 countries have so far pledged to the PRGT and more than 120 countries have pledged to the PRG-HIPC.

sections.label: Separate 21 million SDR limit
sections.summary: The current limit of 21 million SDR before Parliament is a separate contribution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The current limit of 21 million SDR that is before Parliament is a separate contribution.

sections.label: Grants and domestic spending
sections.summary: The contributions do not draw on past Reserves nor affect or reduce any domestic expenditure for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Mr Victor Lye and Mr Saktiandi Supaat both asked if the grants will draw on our past Reserves or reduce domestic spending for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: This set of contributions does not draw on our past Reserves, nor will it affect or reduce any domestic expenditure for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Singapore channels SDR to RST
sections.summary: The IMF announced Singapore will channel 746 million SDR to the RST, joining 22 other countries toward a 33 billion SDR target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Last Wednesday, the IMF announced that Singapore will channel 746 million SDR from the 2021 SDR allocation to the RST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We will join 22 other countries in supporting the IMF to meet its initial fundraising target of 33 billion SDR.

sections.label: IMF loan repayment safeguard
sections.summary: Singapore's IMF loan agreements require the IMF to repay immediately if Singapore has a balance of payments need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Singapore's loan agreements with the IMF include a safeguard that the IMF is obliged to immediately repay the loan in the event Singapore has a balance of payments need.

sections.label: Singapore international aid and institutions
sections.summary: Singapore has given aid including for Cyclone Ditwah and Gaza, and is a founding member of the ADB and World Bank.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In other areas, we have also delivered international aid across the world, such as for Cyclone Ditwah in Sri Lanka last year and most recently, to Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We are also a founding member of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the World Bank.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We have used our unique position as a hub to be a force multiplier, hosting multilateral institutions, such as the ADB, the World Bank, the International Energy Agency, and as Mr Saktiandi pointed out earlier, the IMF-Singapore Regional Training Institute and the IMF Resident Representative Office.
